Madeddu, S., Ueckerdt, F., Pehl, M., Peterseim, J., Lord, M., Kumar, K.A., Krueger, C. and Luderer, G. (2020). The CO2 reduction potential for the European industry via direct electrification of heat supply (power-to-heat). Environmental Research Letters, 15, 124004. https://doi.org/10.1088/1748-9326/abbd02

Locators are printed page numbers (PDF page = printed + 1). A 15-page letter; the supplementary file (sections A.1-A.3, tables A.2) is not in the PDF. Main file (9 technology rows from Table 1, p.5): efficiency (UE output / FE input, printed as fractions 0.50-0.95, recorded in %) or COP (heat pumps 2-5, MVR 3-10, recorded as %), maturity text as state-of-development, application list as description, plasma maximum capacity 7 MW (text p.7). Table 1 is an image: read from a rendered page, numbers legible. The temperature bands are printed only as a colour gradient across four columns (<100, 100-400, 400-1000, >1000 degC), so no temperature numbers are loaded; a qualitative reading is in _other-values (read from chart). Heat pumps and chillers share one row; the COP 2-5 covers both. No costs: the paper states a comprehensive cost analysis of industrial electrification technologies is not available. Electrification shares by sector and stage, the useful-energy split by temperature, and CO2 figures are in _other-values (sector statistics; no technology). Stage figures given as % of useful energy including chemical feedstocks unless stated.

(1) Abstract states 78% of energy demand electrifiable with established technologies (Stage 2) but Sect. 4.2 gives 50% of UE including feedstocks and 78% excluding feedstocks; both loaded. (2) Section 6 says 99% electrification achieved with technologies under development (Stage 3) which excludes feedstocks; 60% includes them. (3) Table 1 efficiency for electric arc furnaces, induction and resistance furnaces is an appliance efficiency, not per tonne.
